A_target.statement:
Let $N \in \Z_{>0}$ and $\omega = e^{2 \pi i / N}$.
The [[Definition:Discrete Fourier Transform|discrete Fourier transform]] $\displaystyle \hat x_k = \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{N - 1} x_n \omega^{-k n}$ satisfies:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{N - 1} \omega^{\paren {j - k} n} = N \delta_{j k}$
:$\widehat {x \circledast y} = \hat x \cdot \hat y$
:$\displaystyle \sum_n \size {x_n}^2 = \frac 1 N \sum_k \size {\hat x_k}^2$
where $\circledast$ is [[Definition:Cyclic Convolution|cyclic convolution]].

B_source.statement: On the [[Definition:Circle Group|circle group]] $\Bbb T$, the exponentials $e^{i k t}$ are [[Definition:Orthogonal (Inner Product Space)|orthogonal]], $\widehat {f * g} = \hat f \cdot \hat g$, and [[Parseval's Theorem]] holds.

substitutions.the circle group: the cyclic group of order N
substitutions.the integral against a character: a finite sum against a root of unity

derived.orthogonality of characters: the geometric sum of a nontrivial root of unity vanishing

validity_conditions: Both settings are harmonic analysis on a compact abelian group, so orthogonality of characters and the convolution theorem follow from the same group-theoretic argument.
Convolution becomes cyclic rather than ordinary, since the group is the cyclic group; forgetting this is the standard source of wraparound error when the transform is used for ordinary convolution.
Convergence questions disappear entirely: all sums are finite, so no analytic hypotheses on the function are needed.
proof_plan: Replace the [[Definition:Circle Group|circle group]] $\Bbb T$ by the [[Definition:Cyclic Group|cyclic group]] $\Z / N \Z$.
Replace the characters $e^{i k t}$ by $n \mapsto \omega^{k n}$, and integration over $\Bbb T$ by summation over $\Z / N \Z$.

For $j \ne k$, by [[Sum of Geometric Sequence]]:
:$\displaystyle \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^{N - 1} \omega^{\paren {j - k} n} = \frac {1 - \omega^{\paren {j - k} N} } {1 - \omega^{j - k} } = 0$
replacing the vanishing integral $\displaystyle \int_{\Bbb T} e^{i \paren {j - k} t} \rd t = 0$.
Parseval follows from orthogonality.
